description: We are a team of six high school students from Almaty, Kazakhstan, passionate about space, Earth science, and building things with real data. Our team combines strong programming and machine learning skills with UI/UX design and visual storytelling, so we can take a project from raw NASA data to a working, polished product.
summary:
About 1.09 million people live within 1 km of the rivers below the glacial lakes of the Ile Alatau, the range above Almaty. These lakes fill and empty within days. The state agency lowers a few of them with siphons each summer, but nobody can visit hundreds of lakes every week, and optical satellites lose them to cloud.

We built GLOFcast, an open web app that reads the whole opening season of NISAR, the new L-band radar of NASA and ISRO (18 June to 25 October 2026), on 659 glacial lakes of the northern Tien Shan, next to Sentinel-1 and optical images. It replays the season week by week: which lake asked for a look, and why. Every lake has a passport: water, history, ground at the dam, ice beside it, snow and lake ice, people living downstream.

What we measured: on 546 lakes that kept their water, Sentinel-1 raised a false "emptying" signal on 96 lakes, NISAR on 30. At Lake Merzbacher, NISAR found a third of the water left eight hours after the last photo of open water. GLOFcast does not forecast outbursts. It shows where to look, and how sure it is.
details:
Web app: https://abzalabdrash.github.io/glofcast-nasa/

Source (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/abzalabdrash/glofcast-nasa

WHAT IT DOES

GLOFcast answers one question for the people who decide which glacial lake gets a visit: which lake needs a look this week, and why.

- It replays the 2026 season in 19 weeks. For each week it lists the lakes that asked for a look, with the reason in plain words, using only data that existed by the end of that week, and shows what happened afterwards.

- Every one of the 659 lakes has a passport of seven lines: water, history, ground at the dam, ice beside the lake, snow and lake ice, people living below, agency reports. Each line names its source and how far it was checked.

- A map shows all lakes, the path the water of each would take, and the towns along it. It works on a phone, with no login.

HOW IT WORKS

1. 659 lake outlines and 311 control patches (lake outlines moved onto flat dry ground).

2. Water from NISAR L2 GCOV (L-band, 20 m): the radar echo inside the outline against a ring of ground around it. We never download a 2 GB granule: scripts read small windows by HTTP range requests, 13.4 GB instead of 408.5 GB.

3. The same number from Sentinel-1 (C-band) and a water share from Sentinel-2, so the two radars are compared on the same lakes.

4. Ground at the dam from NISAR L2 GUNW interferograms; glacier speed beside the lake from NISAR L2 GOFF pixel offsets.

5. People below: flow path on MERIT Hydro and people within 1 km of that river in its first 50 km (GHS-POP), after Taylor et al. 2023.

Every threshold was written down before the catalogue-wide data were pulled.

RESULTS

- NISAR told a full lake from control ground on 648 of 657 lakes, Sentinel-1 on 641. L-band is not sharper than C-band here.

- It is calmer: on 546 lakes that kept their water, Sentinel-1 raised a false "emptying" step on 96 lakes, NISAR on 30.

- Of 9 lakes of 1 ha and more that emptied in 2026, the two radars together caught 8 (7 each). Under 1 ha: none of 4.

- Lake Merzbacher, 17 July 2026: eight hours after the last photo of open water, NISAR found about a third of it left.

- Lake No. 19 above Talgar: the agency ran siphons there in August 2026; both radars recorded the lake losing its water between 19 September and 6 October. About 44,000 people live within 1 km of the river in the first 50 km below it.

- Negative results, kept on the site: 28 of 591 dams move by our rule, and so do 28 of 307 control patches; the small glaciers above Almaty cannot be read in the offset product.

HOW IT WAS CHECKED

Every headline number was computed twice by two separate scripts. Five team members checked the events by eye; each got 14 or 15 of 15 hidden control pictures right.

LIMITS

One season, one region, provisional NISAR products. The people numbers are exposure, not risk. The app replays 2026; it is not yet a weekly service. Nothing here says when a lake will burst.

WHO IT IS FOR

The mudflow protection service of Kazakhstan, hydrologists and local administrations get a short list with a stated reason instead of hundreds of lakes. People living below a lake can read what is known about it.

EARLIER WORK

The lake outlines, the optical record of 2018 to 2026 and the name and map shell of the site come from our earlier project GLOFcast (https://glofcast.org). Everything that uses NISAR and this application were made during the hackathon, 14 and 15 November 2026. Closest prior work by others: THAW (Miles et al., EGU26-16809), on Sentinel-1.

TOOLS

Python (h5py, NumPy, rasterio, shapely, scikit-learn), Google Earth Engine, NASA Earthdata and ASF DAAC; TypeScript, React, Vite, MapLibre GL JS; GitHub Pages.

USE OF SI

The idea, the study area, the questions and every decision were the team's: what to measure, which thresholds to fix before the data, and which results to keep, including the negative ones. Team members checked the events by eye in two rounds. We used an SI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) as a tool under the team's direction: to search the literature, write the data-reading and analysis code, build the web app and draft texts and slides. No image is SI-generated: all are satellite data or charts drawn from data.

NISAR L2 GUNW interferograms, 12-day pairs (ASF DAAC): ground motion at the dams of 591 lakes
NISAR L2 GOFF pixel offsets, 12-day pairs (ASF DAAC): glacier speed beside the lakes
OPERA DSWx-HLS and DSWx-S1 (NASA JPL): NASA water products compared with our lake series
Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 (NASA, USGS): optical looks at Lake Merzbacher
NASA GIBS, Blue Marble: globe imagery of the start page
Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC with NASA Earthdata Login: access to NISAR granules
projectRefs: Sentinel-1 IW GRD (ESA, Copernicus), via Google Earth Engine: C-band brightness of every lake
Sentinel-2 MSI Level-1C (ESA, Copernicus): optical water share, snow and lake ice
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA): slope of control patches
ERA5-Land daily air temperature (ECMWF, Copernicus): temperature context at Merzbacher
NISAR is a joint mission of NASA and ISRO
MERIT Hydro v1.0.1: flow path below each lake
GHS-POP R2023A (European Commission, JRC): people living below each lake
